evidence: src/main/java/com/gymmie/App.java: Minimal JavaFX application entry point loads one FXML view and stylesheet.
src/main/resources/com/gymmie/view/MainWindow.fxml: Small 480x320 starter view containing a single Gymmie label.
checks.notes: Exceptionally small while still demonstrating application, FXML, controller, CSS, and test wiring.

evidence: src/main/resources/com/gymmie/view/MainWindow.fxml: fx:controller, titleLabel, and CSS style classes match the corresponding Java and CSS files.
src/main/java/com/gymmie/App.java: Loads MainWindow.fxml and applies gymmie.css from matching resource paths.
src/main/resources/com/gymmie/css/gymmie.css: Defines the root-pane and title-label classes used by the FXML.
checks.notes: The starter UI is internally consistent; the only limitation is that it intentionally has no user-facing actions beyond initialization.

evidence: README.md: Describes the project as a minimal JavaFX starter and documents run, check, and shadowJar commands present in the build configuration.
AGENTS.md: Lists Java 25, JavaFX 25, Gradle 9.7.1, JUnit, Checkstyle, JaCoCo, and Shadow-related tooling consistent with the repository.
checks.notes: Documentation is clear and mostly accurate, but AGENTS.md says check runs coverage verification even though build.gradle configures JaCoCo reporting without a coverage-verification task.

evidence: src/main/java/com/gymmie/App.java: Application lifecycle and resource loading are separated from the launcher.
src/main/java/com/gymmie/MainController.java: Controller responsibility is limited to initializing the starter view.
src/main/resources/com/gymmie/view/MainWindow.fxml: View structure is kept outside Java code, with CSS separated into its own resource.
checks.notes: The structure is easy for a student to extend; minor duplication of the Gymmie title across App, FXML, and controller is the main maintainability limitation.

summary: The repository is a small, coherent JavaFX scaffold with clear separation of application, view, controller, and CSS. Documentation is mostly accurate, with one overstatement about coverage verification.
